title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the State Forestry Administration, the Ministry of Public Security, and the General Administration of Customs on Issues Concerning the Valuation of Terrestrial Wildlife Products Listed in Appendices I and II of CITES Involved in Criminal Cases of Destruction of Wildlife Resources
keywords_en: smuggling; criminal cases of destroying wildlife resources
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Supreme People's Procuratorate

State Forestry Administration Ministry of Public Security General Administration of Customs

Notice on the Issues Concerning the Valuation of Terrestrial Wildlife Products Listed in CITES Appendix I and Appendix II Involved in Criminal Cases of Destroying Wildlife Resources

Lin Bin Fa [2012] No. 239

To the Higher People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Forestry Departments (Bureaus), and Public Security Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; the People's Procuratorate, Forestry Bureau, and Public Security Bureau of Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps; the Guangdong Sub-Administration of the General Administration of Customs; and all directly subordinate Customs offices:

The People's Republic of China is a State Party to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). Terrestrial wild animals listed in CITES Appendix I and Appendix II that are not native to China have been lawfully approved as Class I and Class II State-protected wild animals, respectively. In recent years, all localities, strictly in accordance with the provisions of CITES and China's laws and regulations on wildlife protection, have investigated and seized a large number of cases involving the illegal purchase, transportation, sale, and smuggling of terrestrial wild animals and their products listed in CITES Appendix I and Appendix II. To ensure that the aforementioned cases are handled according to law, in accordance with Article 24 of the Regulations for the Implementation of the Protection of Terrestrial Wild Animals, Article 4 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases of Smuggling (Fa Shi [2000] No. 30), and Articles 10 and 11 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases of Destroying Wildlife Resources (Fa Shi [2000] No. 37), and with reference to the Notice of the Ministry of Forestry on How to Determine the Value Standard of State Key Protected Wild Animals and Their Products in Wildlife Cases (Lin Ce Tong Zi [1996] No. 8), the value standards for terrestrial wildlife products listed in CITES Appendix I and Appendix II involved in cases of destroying wildlife resources are hereby stipulated as follows:

1. The value of terrestrial wildlife products listed in CITES Appendix I and Appendix II shall be determined by reference to the value standard for similar products of State key protected terrestrial wild animals of the same genus. Where there is no State key protected terrestrial wild animal of the same genus, the value shall be determined by reference to the value standard for similar products of State key protected terrestrial wild animals of the same family. Where there is no State key protected terrestrial wild animal of the same family, the value shall be determined by reference to the value standard for similar products of State key protected terrestrial wild animals of the same order. Where there is no State key protected terrestrial wild animal of the same order, the value shall be determined by reference to the value standard for similar products of State key protected terrestrial wild animals of the same class or phylum.

2. If, within the same genus, family, order, class, or phylum, there are multiple State key protected terrestrial wild animals with different protection levels, the value shall be determined by reference to the value standard for similar products of State key protected terrestrial wild animals of the same protection level within that taxonomic unit. If there are multiple State key protected terrestrial wild animals with the same protection level, the value shall be determined by reference to the value standard for similar products of the State key protected terrestrial wild animal with the lowest value standard within that taxonomic unit. If the taxonomic unit to which the terrestrial wild animal listed in CITES Appendix I or Appendix II belongs contains multiple State key protected terrestrial wild animals but with different protection levels, the value shall be determined by reference to the value standard for similar products of the State key protected terrestrial wild animal with the lowest value standard within that taxonomic unit. If there is only one species of State key protected terrestrial wild animal, the value shall be determined by reference to the value standard for similar products of that species of State key protected terrestrial wild animal.

3. The total value of different parts of the same individual animal seized in the same case shall not exceed the value of that individual animal.

4. If the determined value is lower than the actual transaction price in the illegal trade, the actual transaction price in the illegal trade shall be used for determination.

5. The value of wildlife products such as rhinoceros horn and ivory shall continue to be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Notice of the State Forestry Administration on Issuing the Value Standard for Ivory and Its Products Involved in Smuggling in Criminal Cases of Destroying Wildlife Resources (Lin Bin Fa [2001] No. 234) and the Notice of the State Forestry Administration on Issuing the Value Standard for Rhinoceros Horn Involved in Criminal Cases of Destroying Wildlife Resources (Lin Hu Fa [2002] No. 130).

People's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, customs, and other case-handling units may, in accordance with the above value standards, determine the value of terrestrial wildlife products listed in CITES Appendix I and Appendix II involved in criminal cases of destroying wildlife resources. Where determination is difficult, the competent forestry department at or above the county level, the State Administration for Import and Export of Endangered Species, or its designated appraisal unit shall provide assistance.

This notice is hereby given.

September 17, 2012
